care_plan_ideas: Shot-cycle day cards (on-medication): days 1-2 post-shot = fluids + small salty protein plates + gentle movement, appetite-floor normalization; days 3-5 = the strong days (strength session, protein-floor push); days 6-7 = 'hunger coming back is the medicine's rhythm, not failure' + plan tomorrow's first plate. Requires the one shot-day field.

Protein-rescue anchor: when the floor was missed 2 of the last 3 logged days, tomorrow's ONE THING becomes a named concrete breakfast pulled from plates she has actually logged before (provenance-safe personalization, not a generic 'eat more protein').

Under-fuel evening net as protocol: <2 plates AND <half the protein floor by 18:00 for on-med/post-med → 'something small with protein tonight' + an easy-start next morning; at a 3-day streak, add the one line 'worth mentioning to your prescriber' (no diagnosis, no drug names).

Muscle-preservation week: observed EMA loss faster than ~1%/wk for 2+ weeks with low protein days → auto-propose the existing protein_week WeekIntent + 2 strength sessions in the weekly review, with the mechanism line ('keeps the loss mostly fat').

GI-comfort micro-care keyed to sit-check answers: 'queasy' → cold/bland/salty plate ideas + fluids line; 'backed up' (new chip) → fluids + fiber + a walk; mechanism copy only, never supplements or dosing.

Visit-prep ritual: one optional 'next appointment' date; at T-3 days jeni assembles a 4-week summary (trend, protein days/wk, sit-check pattern, moves) + 'two things worth mentioning' auto-drafted from care events. Consumer retention gold now, and it IS the clinic export seam in disguise.
verdict: Clinically, this is the most correctly-postured consumer app I've seen for a GLP-1-era population: under-fueling is treated as the risk (not the win), protein is the hero, overnight windows carry care tones instead of praise at 16h+, and weekly adaptation is a consented, closed-set, provenance-floored protocol — genuinely the skeleton a medical director could sign. But it is a companion without a chart: it cannot see the medication week that governs its core cohort's body (no shot-day anchor), the subjective observations an NP would actually want (sit-check, under-fuel answers, reflections) evaporate as UserDefaults strings swept at sign-out, and safety flags are frozen at intake even though v6.4 shipped a daily 'overnight fast' completion ring gated entirely on those frozen flags. White-label bones are half-formed — constants are single-sourced but hardcoded, care rules are fused with jeni's prose, and nothing is exportable; a CareProtocol config, an ObservationStore, and a rules/voice split would make Clinic A/B/C a config change without touching a single screen.

keep.what: The fuel-frame inversion + under-eating net for the on-medication chapter
keep.why: Signals.swift:20-22 ('their clinical risk is under-fueling… "first plate landed", never hour arithmetic') and TodayStateBand.swift:120-129 (showsEnoughNet flips the receipt from score to care on <half floor + ≤1 plate) are exactly what I coach GLP-1 patients on between visits; no consumer competitor does this — most celebrate long fasts at this population.

keep.what: WeeklyReview as a consented, closed-set adaptation protocol with provenance floors
keep.why: propose() only speaks protein when ≥4 days actually logged plates (WeeklyReview.swift:226-233), adjustments clamp ±10g/±1 session, and the consented ease applies BEFORE the 1.2-1.6 g/kg advisory clamp (TargetsService.swift:125-127) — this is supervised-titration behavior, and the JSONL ReviewRecord (decision + stampLine + reasonLine) is an audit-trail instinct clinics require.

Every field traces to a stored record, absent fields are omitted not defaulted, and numeric-suppressed cohorts get a rhythm-only view (CoachContextAssembler.swift:8-12, 152-159). Rename two keys and this is a brand-neutral patient-context document — the single best white-label asset in the codebase.

Trend language is silent until 3+ weigh-ins over 5+ days (v5), windows are narrated from real plate timestamps with praise saturating at 14h and 16h+ speaking care (Signals.swift:16-19). That epistemic discipline — never narrating beyond the data — is better than most clinical dashboards I've deployed.

keep.what: ChatSafety as a client-side deterministic pre-filter
keep.why: Crisis/ED language never reaches the model; the fixed care responses carry real resources (988, NEDA) in-register (CoachContextAssembler.swift:225-258). Client-side deterministic routing is the correct architecture placement — it just needs to write state (see problems).

problems.title: Safety state is intake-frozen while fasting-completion UI shipped on top of it
problems.evidence: ChatSession.swift:197-203: an ED-marker hit yields the care response + Analytics.track only — no flag written. CohortStore.swift:134-139: onb_restrictive_food 'becomes writable via safety surfaces later' (never built); safety_numeric_suppression written only by the onboarding gate (OV5ScreensNumbers.swift:555-575). Meanwhile screenshot 01 / TodayView.swift:466-478,533-551 show the v6.4 'overnight fast' row with a check ring that marks done at ≥12h, gated solely by QuietHours.mayNarrate = !isRestrictiveRisk && !isNumericSuppressed (QuietHours.swift:88-90).
problems.detail: Screening that never re-screens is the first thing a clinic medical director rejects, and here it is a live consumer risk too: restriction risk in women 22-35 typically emerges or surfaces AFTER intake. A user who tells jeni about purge behavior tonight gets NEDA once, then tomorrow the app resumes full numerals and a daily fast-completion ring, because detection (ChatSafety) and state (CohortStore flags) are disconnected. The entire safety weight of the fast ring rests on two answers frozen at onboarding.

problems.title: The app is medication-blind for its on-medication cohort — no shot-day anchor, no titration state
problems.evidence: CohortStore.swift:79-92: appetiteRhythmKey ('after_shot / late_week / most_days / varies') is asked once at onboarding and frozen; medicationStatusKey is a static category. Repo-wide grep finds zero dose-day/injection-day/missed-dose fields. Signals.swift's fuel-frame inversion knows she's on medication but not WHERE in the medication week she is.
problems.detail: The GLP-1 week is a physiologic waveform — appetite floor and nausea peak days 1-2 post-injection, hunger returning days 5-7 — and it is the #1 topic of my between-visit inbox ('is it normal that…'). The app already asks 'when is appetite loudest' but can never say 'day 2 after your shot — small plates sit best' or 'hunger today is the rhythm, not failure', and sit-check answers can't be correlated to the cycle. This is the gap between GLP-1-aware copy and GLP-1-native care, and it also blocks the clinically-useful visit summary (side effects by cycle position).

problems.title: Subjective observations are disposable — the data the next clinic visit needs has no store
problems.evidence: day.sit (fine/heavy/queasy) and day.reflection are UserDefaults strings (TodayStateBand.swift:115-118, 291) swept at sign-out (AppSync.swift:1036-1050 scopedPrefixes 'day.sit.', 'day.note.'); WeeklyReview records are device-local JSONL in Application Support (WeeklyReview.swift:346-353) — lost on device change; no aggregation reads sit history beyond yesterday (DailyBriefEngine.Context.yesterdaySat).
problems.detail: Weight got a real store (userId-scoped SwiftData, synced); how she FELT did not. An NP at the next visit wants interval weights (collected, excellent), protein adequacy days (computed weekly, then discarded as prose), side-effect frequency (one word, yesterday only), and mood pattern (evaporates). Because nothing persists as typed observations, 'queasy 3 of the last 7 evenings' is uncomputable, jeni has no week-scale memory of her answers, and her signed program history (ReviewRecords) silently dies with the phone. This is the missing foundation under red-flags, export, and coach memory alike.

problems.title: No red-flag rule layer over data the app already computes
problems.evidence: snapshot.emaDelta7dKg exists (CoachContextAssembler.swift:128) but no rule checks observed rate-of-loss — all lossRate machinery is plan-side floors/caps (ProgramGoalCalculator.swift:150-166, IntensityProfile). proteinDays7 and loggedDays7 feed the brief (DailyBriefEngine.swift:70-73) but the muscle-loss signature (fast observed loss + low protein days) — named explicitly in the founder's north star — is never detected. showsEnoughNet is daily-copy-only; no streak memory, no record when care-tone copy fires.
problems.detail: The founder brief promises 'notices patterns before she does (muscle-loss risk…)'. Today every care-worthy pattern at most bends one day's copy and leaves no trace. A clinic deployment needs each fire to exist as a record with severity + provenance + disposition (a CareEvent), so triage routing later is a subscription to existing events, not a new engine. The consumer UI can keep exactly today's gentle register — the record is the invisible seam.

problems.title: Care rules and brand voice are fused inside the engines
problems.evidence: ReviewProposal.title/.reason are jeni-voice lowercase strings inside the enum (WeeklyReview.swift:104-127); propose() embeds prose next to clinical clamps ('a 5g lower floor fits this week', WeeklyReview.swift:228-247); DailyBriefEngine.brief() returns fused line/italic/chatSeed prose (DailyBriefEngine.swift:104+); Signals week-pick outputs bake copy + chatSeed together (Signals.swift:780-843).
problems.detail: To change one sentence for Clinic B (or Spanish, or a different persona) you fork the clinical rule that contains it. The typed Context structs going IN are already brand-neutral — the entanglement is only on the way out. Emitting typed outcomes (kind + params + provenance facts) and rendering strings in a brand-owned voice layer preserves jeni byte-for-byte as the default renderer while unfusing the care logic.

problems.title: No exportable interval summary despite computing one every week
problems.evidence: ProgramWeekSlice assembles kept days, plate count, protein-days-met, weigh count, moved days per week (WeeklyReview.swift:36-79, weekSlice loader 419-501) — then renders one sentence (weekStory) and discards. The only share surface in the app is the lesson quote card. 02_COHESION.md's held-for-next-round list confirms the review doesn't yet reference the signal week.
problems.detail: Most GLP-1 users see a prescriber monthly; 'bring your last 4 weeks' is both a consumer trust/retention move and the clinic-visibility seam with near-zero new math — the summary struct already exists, it just isn't persisted or renderable as an artifact. Care-team visibility later becomes an opt-in sync policy on records that already exist, not a new pipeline.

problems.title: Sit-check vocabulary is one side effect wide, one cohort narrow
problems.evidence: TodayStateBand.swift:193-203: chips are exactly 'fine / heavy / queasy', rendered only when chapter == .onMedication, evening only. Constipation — the most persistent GLP-1 complaint in my panel and the one that outlasts titration — is unrepresentable; post-medication cohort gets no sit-check at all.
problems.detail: The interaction design is right (one optional tap, skipped-forever-is-fine); the vocabulary and gating undersell it. One added chip ('backed up') and extending to the post-medication chapter would make this the app's only true side-effect stream — provided answers land in a real store (problem 3).

problems.title: GLP-1 protein clamp exceeds its own cited advisory band for smaller women
problems.evidence: TargetsService.swift:128-135: lo = 90.0 for GLP-1-current forces ≥90g; at 50kg that is 1.8 g/kg, above the 1.2-1.6 '4-society advisory band' the doc comment cites (lines 119-121). The 22-35 female audience includes many 48-58kg users.
problems.detail: Not a safety issue for healthy kidneys, but the code claims the advisory band clamps the floor and it doesn't at the low end. Fix inside the future CareProtocol config pass: floor = min(90, round5(1.6 × kg)) or an explicit small-body branch — one line, keeps the comment honest for any future clinical review.

recommendations.title: Anchor the medication week: one optional shot-day field, read by every engine
recommendations.detail: Collect a weekday ('which day is your shot day? · optional · change anytime') + an optional 'dose changed recently?' tri-state for the self-reported on-medication cohort, in Settings or the first-week flow — a weekday is not a brand name and food/hydration copy is not dosing advice, so compliance floors hold. Derive dayInMedicationWeek and feed: DailyBriefEngine (day 1-2: 'small plates and fluids sit best today'; day 5-7: 'hunger coming back is the rhythm, not failure'), the fuel-frame in Signals, sit-check correlation ('queasy has landed the two days after your shot'), and WeeklyReview provenance. Never prescriptive, never predictive beyond her own reported anchor. This one field converts the core cohort's experience from GLP-1-aware to GLP-1-native and is the spine side-effects, red-flags, and visit-prep all hang from.

recommendations.title: ObservationStore: one typed, userId-scoped, append-only record store
recommendations.detail: A SwiftData ObservationRecord (kind, dayKey, value, provenance, userId, createdAt) absorbing day.sit, day.reflection, enough-net answers, tonight-plan, care events, and ReviewRecords (retiring the UserDefaults strings and the device-local JSONL). Per-kind sync policy, defaulting to local-only — nothing changes for the user today, but observations become aggregatable (streak rules), portable (survive device change like weight logs already do), exportable (visit summary), and the sign-out sweep collapses to one store drop. This is the invisible clinic seam: a future care-team view is a sync-policy flip on records that already exist, not a new data model.

recommendations.title: Live CareState: let evidence written after intake move the safety flags
recommendations.detail: Three wire points: (1) an ED-marker ChatSafety hit sets a pending care flag; next morning jeni offers, in-register, 'want the numbers to rest for a while?' — consent sets safety_numeric_suppression / restrictive-risk (CohortStore.swift:134-139 already anticipates writable safety surfaces), which auto-retracts the fast ring and numerals via the existing mayNarrate gate; (2) a crisis routing makes the next brief acknowledge gently and surfaces BreakState; (3) every routing appends an ObservationStore care event so it is never a silent one-off. Closes the intake-frozen hole that currently carries the entire weight of the v6.4 fast-completion ring.

recommendations.title: Quiet red-flag rules as CareEvents over streams the app already holds
recommendations.detail: Three deterministic rules, all computable today: (a) observed EMA loss > ~1%/wk sustained 2+ weeks AND proteinDays7 low → WeeklyReview proposes the existing protein_week intent + strength emphasis (02_COHESION.md already names signal-informed re-signing as held work); (b) 3+ consecutive under-fuel days (the showsEnoughNet condition, given streak memory) → a check-in line; (c) sit-check 'queasy'/'heavy' ≥3 of 7 → one line: 'worth mentioning to your prescriber' — no diagnosis, no drug names. Each fire appends a CareEvent (severity, provenance, disposition) to the ObservationStore; the UI keeps today's register exactly. This cashes the north star's 'notices before she does' AND builds the triage substrate a clinic subscribes to later.

recommendations.title: CareProtocol: gather every clinical constant into one injected, reviewable config
recommendations.detail: One Codable struct holding protein g/kg by cohort + clamps (TargetsService.swift:131-134), pace floors/caps (ProgramGoalCalculator.swift:150-166), window tone thresholds 12/14/16h (Signals.swift:43-50), band zones 1.4/2.3kg (BandModel), review knobs ±10g/±1 (WeeklyReview.swift:153-156, 290-298), and the new red-flag thresholds. `.default` == today's shipped values, engines read the injected protocol, tests assert behavior-identical. Zero user-visible change; produces the single artifact a medical director reviews and signs; Clinic A/B/C becomes a protocol instance. Fix the <56kg protein-floor band violation while touching it.

recommendations.title: Split rules from voice, starting with WeeklyReview
recommendations.detail: ReviewProposal drops its inline title/reason strings and carries kind + params + provenance facts; a BrandVoice renderer (jeni's exact current strings as the default implementation) produces the prose. Then DailyBriefEngine (its Context input is already brand-neutral — only brief()'s output fuses). Per-engine, opportunistic, byte-identical output under the default renderer. Unlocks white-label voice and localization, and lets the founder iterate jeni's register without ever touching a clinical rule again.

recommendations.title: Visit-prep summary: persist week slices, add one optional appointment date
recommendations.detail: Persist the ProgramWeekSlice computed at each re-signing as a record; add an optional 'next appointment' date field; at T-3 days jeni offers a 4-week summary (trend + rate, protein days/wk, sit-check pattern, sessions, kept days) plus 'two things worth mentioning' drafted from care events. Renderable as an in-app card now, a share-PDF later. Directly improves the next clinic visit for today's consumer users and quietly becomes the exportable-summary seam a clinic deployment requires.

recommendations.title: Widen the sit-check one chip and one cohort
recommendations.detail: Add 'backed up' to fine/heavy/queasy (constipation is the most persistent GLP-1 complaint and the one that outlasts titration), extend the evening sit-check to the post-medication chapter, keep it one optional tap, and store answers in the ObservationStore so streaks are computable. This makes the app's only side-effect stream clinically legible at a cost of one word.

one_transformative_move: Give the app the medication week: one optional shot-day field (plus observation memory of how days sat), read by every engine — the brief, the fuel frame, the sit-check, the weekly review. Today the app tracks what she does; with a shot-day anchor it anticipates what her body's week is about to do ('day 2 — small plates sit best', 'day 6 — hunger returning is the rhythm, not failure'), which is precisely the felt experience of 'Jeni is already paying attention' for the cohort this product is converging on, and it is the spine that side-effect capture, muscle-loss red flags, and prescriber visit-prep all hang from — each of which is otherwise structurally impossible.
